A heading that is quite long and must never be wrapped even when narrow

Markdown files are often wrapped at seventy-two columns so that they read comfortably in terminals and produce small diffs. The wrapper must never break a line where the next word would start a new block, such as - a dash, + a plus sign, 1. a number with a period, or # a hash.

Quoted text is wrapped too, with the quote prefix accounted for in the available width of each line.

  • List items wrap with a hanging indent that lines up under the first character of the item text.
  • Short item.

Links like this one with a long URL keep their destination intact, and code spans stay whole.

Code blocks are never wrapped, no matter how long their lines are, because whitespace in code is significant.
